coverage: Saturday 29 Aug 2026 weekend run (~07:02-07:55 SGT). All tracked markets (US, HK, SG, JP, KR) are closed. Latest completed session is Friday 28 Aug for the US (S&P 500 7,711.76 -0.25%, Nasdaq 26,402 -0.52%, VIX 14.43 -0.55%); latest completed session in the price feed for HK/JP/KR/SG is Thursday 27 Aug (Friday's Asia bar had not yet consolidated at fetch time -- a normal lag, not a holiday). Friday's dominant, portfolio-defining event was Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish debut Jackson Hole keynote, which triggered a sharp rout in gold, silver, miners, rare earths and crypto while broad US equities and credit barely reacted.
tldr: Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole debut ("we have work to do" on inflation, no forward guidance) pushed September hike odds from ~36% to ~57-58% and triggered the levered silver/gold-miners sleeve's largest single-day drawdown in months: SLV -4.38%, GLD -3.24%, silver miners -3.6% to -4.9%.

Broad US equities and credit shrugged it off entirely -- S&P -0.25%, Nasdaq -0.52%, VIX barely moved (-0.55% to 14.43) -- confirming this was a rates/dollar-driven 'debasement trade' unwind, not a broad risk-off event.

Rare earths (MP -4.91%, UUUU -6.80%) and crypto (BTC -3.18%, ~$481M liquidations) also sold off hard as high-beta extensions of the same shock, though the rare-earth causation is only moderately confirmed this run.

Model regime downgraded from 'risk-on confirmed, modest OW across equities/commodities/crypto' to 'Neutral equities/commodities, UW crypto, OW USD/cash' -- a genuine, if likely temporary, repricing rather than a fundamental break in the precious-metals bull case.
Berkshire's Greg Abel deployed a further ~$10B into Alphabet and resumed buybacks (first since June 2024); Ackman launched an evergreen pre-IPO retail-access fund (Pershing Square Ventures).

Global equity funds snapped a 13-week inflow streak into a -$5.87bn outflow (wk to 26 Aug) as gold funds hit a 6-month inflow high (+$4.21bn) -- flow positioning was already rotating defensive right before Friday's shock landed.

Investors: re-verified, no new 13F cycle (Q3 not due until 16 Nov 2026); folded in the same post-13F whale news as intel.json.

Model: macro regime rewritten around Friday's hawkish Warsh shock -- Equity/Commodities downgraded Neutral, Crypto downgraded UW, USD/Cash upgraded OW; 25 of 49 calls deep-updated (metals, miners, rare earths, crypto, bonds, USO/XLE, broad equity indices, XLF), remaining 24 adjusted directionally.

Market: Fear&Greed recalibrated to ~55/Neutral (from 58/Greed); breadth shows a genuinely balanced Friday session (net-positive 52wk highs/lows) despite the metals headline stress; flows updated to the week-to-26-Aug Lipper/BofA data showing the first equity-fund outflow in 13 weeks and an accelerating gold-fund inflow.

News: 13 fresh items led by the Warsh/gold-rout story and its follow-through (BLS benchmark revision, crypto selloff, rare-earth weakness), plus SG banks/UOB-Allianz deal, Hongkong Land's Wheelock Place close, and Hormuz/oil geopolitics.

Flows-investors: Korea extended with two new confirmed sessions (27-28 Aug) showing a Friday reversal to foreign/institutional selling; Japan, Hong Kong, China, Singapore and US carried forward with discrepancies/gaps explicitly flagged rather than papered over.

regime.label: Hawkish Warsh debut jolts gold/silver/crypto; broad equities and credit shrug it off -- a rates-driven correction, not a risk-off event
regime.oneLiner: Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole debut repriced September hike odds to ~58% and hit the debasement trade hard, but equities and credit show no confirmation of a broader risk-off shift.
